text:
alex: FYI customer hitting 429 + occasional 503s when they burst above their expected qps on Dedicated pool.
maria: Which pool and which SLA? can you paste the request id or sample timestamps?
alex: pool: eu-west-1-ded-42, customer tenant: acme-inc, example req id: rID:cf3a2f2a. Errors start ~2026-03-15T14:03:10Z, repeat on spikes.
kevin: Do they have reserved tokens configured? Could be reserved pool exhausted and fallback to shared capacity which is throttling.
alex: They have a small reserved commit (2k qps sustained) but say they briefly spike to 10k qps. We expect automatic burst to reserved pool burst capacity.
maria: Can you repro locally with the same headers? ask them to send a short repro: 5s ramp to 10k qps.
alex: I ran a quick synthetic to mimic headers and API key — here's the curl pattern I used:

```
# heat test (do NOT run against production without notice)
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  curl -s -X POST \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-TEST" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":"test"}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
wait
```

kevin: Nice. What did the stream show? logs?
alex: Sampling of server logs around the spike:

```
[2026-03-15T14:03:11.128Z] pool=eu-west-1-ded-42 tenant=acme state=reserved_tokens=0 burst_allowed=false action=throttle code=429 rID=cf3a2f2a
[2026-03-15T14:03:12.402Z] pool=eu-west-1-ded-42 tenant=acme state=reserved_tokens=0 fallback=shared_pool action=drop code=503 rID=cf3a2f2a
[2026-03-15T14:03:12.889Z] pool=eu-west-1-ded-42 tenant=acme rule=ratecap mismatch=route_limit(5k)<tenant_request(10k) action=cap_enforce
```

maria: That last line is interesting — route-level rate limit lower than tenant desired burst. Could be policy mismatch: route config or per-model cap.
kevin: Agreed. Two hypotheses: 1) route has a conservative hard cap (5k) enforced to meet SLA across tenants; 2) our burst accounting didn't credit the reserved burst tokens (bug). We need quick repro with headers that hit the route and model used (rwd-3b) and the exact route path.
alex: Customer reports they call /v1/generate with model=rwd-3b and include application route header: X-Route-Tag: recommender. I reproduced with that header and saw consistent 429s once sustained >5k rps.
kevin: Can you run this minimal repro and capture response headers? we want x-rw-rate, x-rw-pool, x-rw-tenant-tokens.

```
# single-client ramp repro
ab -n 2000 -c 200 -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-TEST" -H "X-Route-Tag: recommender" \
  -p post.json -T application/json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

alex: Done. Key headers from a 429 response:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rate: 5000/5000
x-rw-pool: eu-west-1-ded-42
x-rw-tenant-tokens: 0
retry-after: 1
```

maria: That confirms route cap is 5k and tenant had 0 reserved tokens at time. Did they consume tokens earlier in the window? could be token bucket refill rate slower than expected.
kevin: We should check reserved_pools config for acme-inc and the route policy mapping. I’ll pull config: reserved_commit=2000, burst_allowance=8000, route_soft_cap=5000.
alex: So config says burst_allowance 8k but route_soft_cap 5k — that's the mismatch. Customer assumed they could burst to 10k but route cap blocks above 5k.
maria: Action items:
- Kevin: validate whether burst tokens are being correctly counted and whether reserved burst should bypass route soft cap (policy doc) — prioritise this. (assigned)
- Alex: reply to customer with repro findings and recommend temporary workaround: use alternate route tag or schedule controlled ramp, or escalate to dedicated-config change. (assigned)
- Kevin: if policy intends reserved burst to bypass route caps, open infra bug SR with logs above and tag urgent. include sample request/headers.

kevin: I'll open SR-7421 (infra) and paste logs + repro commands. Also will check whether this affects other tenants on same pool.
alex: Customer reply: "Thanks — if we need to change route tag we can, but we need guaranteed burst for end-of-day jobs. Can you confirm SLA for burst?"
maria: SLA note: committed throughput is guaranteed; burst is best-effort within pool and subject to route-level caps and overall pool headroom. We should be explicit.
kevin: For now propose two paths: 1) increase route soft cap for their route (requires config change + canary), 2) bump reserved commit for predictable capacity. I'll prepare estimated cost/delta.
alex: Customer accepted schedule for config change canary. I'll schedule a canary on 2026-03-17 02:00Z and will notify support before deploy.
support-bot: Deploybot scheduled canary: infra-config-change SR-7421 -> canary window 2026-03-17T02:00:00Z to 2026-03-17T03:00:00Z. :white_check_mark:
kevin: I'll also add monitoring alert to track x-rw-rate against route cap and pool headroom during canary.

maria: Good. Documenting repro steps in the ticket so QA can validate. Also note: if we change route cap, run A/B with fallback model variant rwd-3b-quant to measure latency/cost.
alex: Thanks team. I'll update customer and close loop after canary results.
kevin: SR-7421 created: https://redwood.internal/sr/7421 — added logs and repro steps.
alex: marking follow-up for 2026-03-17: post-canary status.
oncall-bot: Reminder scheduled: follow-up with customer 2026-03-17T04:00:00Z.
